title: `st.dataframe` crashes with maximum update depth exceeded
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Updating tables on the sidebar makes the browser go crazy and eventually crash due to maximum update depth exceeded.
* Browser is unresponsive
* Adjusting the width of the sidebar makes the problem go away (sometimes)
* Some tables just crash before even the first render
* This has been happening for a while (min 3 months)

[Screencast from 2024-01-12 11-38-00.webm](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/100993/329f43b0-3c02-4cd8-95d5-5b8e4ba88630)

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/100993/6507adb9-d666-4247-82a4-7f7859154653)



### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
with st.sidebar:
  container = st.empty()

while True:
  container.dataframe(...)
  time.sleep(1)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.2x
- Python version: irrelevant
- Operating System: irrelevant
- Browser: blink

The issue will get fixed in `1.31` by https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/7779

Also experiencing this problem periodically with version 1.33.0! 

I have a multi-page application with roughly 5-10 st.dataframe()'s on display. They pretty much all have _use_container_width=True_, but weirdly only a couple seem to return the React error. Using the @st.cache_data() decorator also helps, but for frequently updating data this is kind of annoying. The tables themselves are pretty small, max of 800 rows in one table and every other table is like 10-30 rows. Would appreciate any help on this!

comments.author: participant15
comments.body:
I have the same problem on streamlit version 1.36.0

I can't share my actual code, but it is a dataframe displayed in a container, in a tab, in a column, something like this:

```python
column_1, column_2 = st.columns(2)
tab_a, tab_b, tab_c, tab_d = column_2.tabs("a", "b", "c", "d")
for df in dfs:  # dfs are different columns of a much wider dataframe
  styled_df = df.style.apply(style, axis=1)  # applying a style by row
  container = tab_a.container
  # table_height is calculated from a select_box shown below the table, which is why the dataframe is in a container
  container.dataframe(styled_df, use_container_width=True, hide_index=True, height=table_height)
```

The error only occurs for the dataframe in tab_a. The error **only occurs when the site is deployed, ie not when running locally**. The error only occurs when an option to hide a few other arbitrary containers (st.markdown and st.tabs) is checked, i.e. the dataframe displays correctly when the site launches, but breaks after a user interaction with another element.

The dataframes are similar, but not exactly the same. The dataframes all have 59 rows. The dataframe in tab_a and tab_d has 6 columns. The dataframe in tab_b has 1 column, and the dataframe in tab_c has 3 columns. They all contain variants of the same or related data, i.e. the first column (a pseudo index column) is the same in all four dataframes. The dataframe in tab_a has one styling component (a few values in one column can be colored) that is not applied to the other three dataframes.

It is difficult to troubleshoot the issue because it doesn't occur locally, and I have no access to the server it is deployed on at the moment.

comments.body:
In my case this error was related to:
- using st.container to store other objects like st.dataframe
- having zoomed out browser window (80%) (user's resolution 1366x768)
- Chrome/Edge (did not check other browsers)
- streamlit 1.38
Having those conditions in check I encountered error in code below if I refreshed app.

1. Error generating app
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import streamlit as st
def load_data():
    df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.rand(100, 5), columns=[f'col_{i}' for i in range(1, 6)])
    
    # Add a categorical column with two categories 'A' and 'B'
    df['category'] = np.random.choice(['Category A', 'Category B'], size=len(df))
    
    # Add a date column with random dates between a given range
    date_range = pd.date_range(start='2023-01-01', end='2024-01-01', periods=len(df))
    df['random_dates'] = np.random.choice(date_range, size=len(df))
    return df

if __name__ == "__main__":
    df = load_data()
    container = st.container()
    container.dataframe(
        df,
        use_container_width=True
        )
``` 


2. Slightly changed app without errors
```python

if __name__ == "__main__":
``` 

comments.body:
Good news :<nick>:: After many hours of trying various things to reproduce this issue, I finally got to a setup that allows me to reproduce it in almost every rerun with a very specific setup: an old monitor set to a 1280 x 720 resolution, with the tab being zoomed out to 75%, and a script containing lots of dataframes with `use_container_width=True` & vertical scrolling in different containers (sidebar, columns, popover, tabs) :<nick>: Finally, there is some hope to fully fixing this soon :<nick>:

Thanks to everyone here for all the input! Especially to @participant22 & @participant21 for the hints on the resolution.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: The fix for the issue will be released on Streamlit 1.39 🚀 If anyone still runs into this issue with >= 1.39, please write in this thread or open a new issue.
